_comment: The `gnomon compliance dataflow --json` document, schema gnomon.dataflow/2, and the
residency rule it reports on: [compliance] allowed_regions in policy.toml and
A kind, side, source, locality or key added or renamed, or an exit moved, is a contract
change: packages/gnomon-cli/src/dataflow.test.ts asserts these lists against the code
and real reports, and packages/gnomon-core/src/residency.test.ts the rule.

exit_codes.0: every declared route is admitted, or no residency rule is declared
exit_codes.2: the residency rule refuses or closed a route (a primary refused when its role runs, a fallback or escalation dropped, a non-local shadow switched off)

host_agent: another harness governed here by gnomon guard: its hook installed (guard status, any state but not_installed) or its calls seen by the guard. gnomon decides its tool calls but does not route its model requests, so host, locality, region and region_source are null; residency.outside names each one, and the compliance probe residency_held does not hold while there is one

rule.admitted: a loopback URL (this machine), or an endpoint whose declared region is in allowed_regions (case-insensitive)
rule.refused_primary: resolveEndpoint throws naming the endpoint, host and rule; the role does not run
rule.closed_side: a fallback or escalation outside the rule is dropped and the role runs without it (config.residency.closed)
rule.shadow: a [shadow] off this machine is switched off (config.residency.shadow_closed)
rule.override: GNOMON_MODEL_URL off this machine is refused
rule.undeclared: a private-network or remote host with no declared region is refused: a URL never decides a region
rule.no_rule: without allowed_regions every route is built exactly as before; region is only a declaration
